ratio to the (0,1)-stratum mean; bars +/- 1 SD over curves; 165 curves x 4 subspaces
B. n = 51 ordinary class, f_pi = 49, ell = 7: |F| per level
114 vertices; cofactor 2827441512; 2-sum yield / |F|^2 is constant to 5 digits
C. n = 16, m = 3 panel: reductions per call
production S4 solver, 6 probes per curve, monomial V; 13/13 cells
D. Transport cost vs rho across the Koblitz ladder (log2 F_q multiplications, cost model in transport_cost_table.py)

bars: transport (kernel route construction + two evaluations); red marks: rho on a floor curve (negation only); blue marks: rho on the crater (signed Frobenius); grey: kernel field degree too large to construct

Reading: wherever the descending isogeny is constructible, transport costs far less than rho on either curve, so a floor-curve method must beat the crater's rho to matter (H3); where the kernel field is huge (grey / dashed), neither direction is reachable and the levels are not known to be DLP-equivalent (JMV's open case).
